style.shading: smooth gradient shading from one warm key light (top-left), lighter top faces, darker sides, soft contact shadows, vignette
style.shape_language: characters are a huge sphere head (about half the height) on a small tube body with stick arms ending in ball hands and stick legs ending in ball shoes; furniture and machines are simple boxes and cylinders; cone lamps

style.type_ui: bold sans text on in-world objects (screens, signs, papers, calendars) carries every number; captions one word at a time, uppercase heavy white with a black outline, centred at about 73% of the height
style.motion_style: snappy cartoon acting: quick expression changes (eyes popping to rings, brows jumping, sweat drops), small body moves; slow push-ins; whip pans between angles
style.signature: the money shots are full-frame inserts of papers and screens with the key number on a yellow highlight; wall calendars mark time; reaction close-ups of the huge face
style.do_not_copy: the topic (a junk-mail cheque deposited at a bank), the bank, cheque, ATM, safe-deposit room, the dollar figures, dates and any words on screen; the creator handle or watermark

story.summary: A man deposits a junk-mail sample cheque as a joke, the bank pays out, he keeps every cent untouched until the bank comes for it, and he trades it back for a written apology.
story.hook: The first line gives the whole absurd outcome with its dollar figure while the hero stands at the machine, then the balance and a shocked take.
highlights: 0-6 s: outcome first, then flashback: the viewer knows the punchline and wants the how
13-21 s: inserts of the paper with the number and the fine print highlighted as it is read: proof on screen
25-26 s: one-word line "What." on a reaction take, deadpan rhythm
33-35 s: a question to the viewer ("so what does he do?") answered with "Nothing." - the unexpected choice
47-64 s: "you see" reveal of what he knew, then a deadpan punchline as the last line
